method: Composite of Sight & Sound 2022 critics' poll (top 250, BFI), TSPDT 2026 '1,000 Greatest Films' (eligible top 150 subset), and AFI's 100 Years...100 Movies (2007, US-only, weighted 0.5x to limit its national bias). Scored by weighted normalized rank (TSPDT 1.0x, S&S 1.3x, AFI 0.5x), summed per film. New candidates not in the TSPDT base pool were added only where ranked in the S&S top 150. Eligibility: a film is excluded only if its production, direction AND principal cast are all from Africa, Latin America, South/Southeast Asia or the Middle East; excluded from this edition on that basis: Pather Panchali, Black Girl, Touki Bouki, The House Is Black, Tropical Malady, Close-Up. Tie-break: composite score, then earlier year. NOT YET MERGED: Cahiers du Cinema list (no clean single ranked list located), Kinema Junpo, other national polls -- flagged here rather than silently omitted.

films.title: Citizen Kane
films.synopsis: A reporter investigates the last word of a dead newspaper tycoon. Interviews with those who knew him assemble a portrait of a man built on ambition and image.
films.why: Reset the grammar of cinema with deep focus, nonlinear structure and overlapping sound.

films.title: Vertigo
films.synopsis: A retired detective with a fear of heights is hired to follow a friend's wife. His assignment pulls him into an obsession with her.
films.why: Hitchcock's most psychologically exposed work; it overtook Kane in Sight & Sound's 2012 poll.

films.title: The Godfather
films.synopsis: The patriarch of a New York crime family sees his empire threatened. His youngest son, an outsider to the business, is drawn into it.
films.why: Merged popular appeal with critical standing like few films before it.

films.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
films.synopsis: A mysterious monolith shapes human history from prehistory to the space age. A crewed mission to Jupiter is guided by an advanced computer.
films.why: Set the visual and philosophical standard for serious science fiction.

films.title: Singin' in the Rain
films.synopsis: A silent-film star faces the arrival of sound pictures in late-1920s Hollywood. A young singer and a stubborn co-star complicate the transition.
films.why: The benchmark Hollywood musical and a loving portrait of the industry.

films.title: The Searchers
films.synopsis: After a raid destroys his brother's family, a Civil War veteran searches for his missing niece across years of frontier territory.
films.why: The most debated and influential western, cited by many later directors.

films.title: Apocalypse Now
films.synopsis: During the Vietnam War, a captain is sent up a jungle river to find a rogue colonel. The journey grows stranger the deeper he goes.
films.why: The defining Vietnam-era epic, notable for its sound design and production legend.

films.title: Psycho
films.synopsis: A secretary leaves town with stolen money and stops at an isolated motel. Its quiet owner seems pleasant enough.
films.why: Reshaped the horror-thriller and the way films handle audience expectation.

films.title: City Lights
films.synopsis: A tramp befriends a blind flower seller. He tries to find money to help her while keeping up appearances.
films.why: Often cited as Chaplin's finest balance of comedy and sentiment.

films.title: Taxi Driver
films.synopsis: A lonely Vietnam veteran takes a night job driving a cab in New York. The city's grime feeds his growing isolation.
films.why: A landmark of 1970s American cinema and of Scorsese's career.

films.title: Some Like It Hot
films.synopsis: Two musicians witness a crime in Prohibition-era Chicago. They flee by joining an all-women band heading to Florida.
films.why: Regularly voted among the greatest comedies ever made.

films.title: Tokyo Story
films.synopsis: An elderly couple travel to Tokyo to visit their grown children. The children are too busy to spend much time with them.
films.why: The summit of Ozu's quiet, low-angle style and a perennial top-ten entry.

films.title: Casablanca
films.synopsis: In wartime Morocco, a cynical club owner holds letters of transit that many want. An old love arrives at his door.
films.why: The enduring example of Hollywood studio-era craft and quotability.

films.title: Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles
films.synopsis: Over three days, a widowed housewife follows a precise domestic routine. Small deviations begin to appear.
films.why: Topped Sight & Sound's 2022 critics' poll as the first film by a woman to do so.

films.title: The Rules of the Game
films.synopsis: Aristocrats and their servants gather for a weekend at a country estate. Romantic entanglements multiply across both floors of the house.
films.why: Its ensemble staging and social satire influenced generations of directors.

films.title: Sunrise: A Song of Two Humans
films.synopsis: A farmer is tempted by a woman from the city. A journey with his wife tests what remains of their marriage.
films.why: A peak of silent-era visual storytelling made in Hollywood by a German master.

films.title: In the Mood for Love
films.synopsis: In 1962 Hong Kong, two neighbours discover their spouses are connected. Their own meetings become careful and restrained.
films.why: The most acclaimed film of the 21st century in several polls; a high point of modern style.

films.title: Seven Samurai
films.synopsis: A village menaced by bandits hires masterless samurai to defend it. The unlikely group must train farmers to fight.
films.why: Established the template for the team-assembly action film.

films.title: Man with a Movie Camera
films.synopsis: A cameraman moves through a Soviet city from dawn to night. The film shows both the life of the city and the machinery of filmmaking.
films.why: Placed on Sight & Sound's list as a landmark of the avant-garde documentary.

films.title: Rear Window
films.synopsis: A photographer confined to his apartment watches his neighbours across the courtyard. He begins to suspect something is wrong.
films.why: A model of suspense through point of view.

films.title: Persona
films.synopsis: A nurse is assigned to care for an actress who has stopped speaking. Isolated together, their identities begin to blur.
films.why: Bergman's most formally daring film and a touchstone of modernist cinema.

films.title: 8½
films.synopsis: A film director in creative crisis retreats to a spa while his production stalls. Memory, fantasy and desire crowd his attention.
films.why: The definitive film about the act of making films.

films.title: Mulholland Dr.
films.synopsis: An aspiring actress arrives in Los Angeles and meets a woman suffering from amnesia. Together they try to piece together who she is.
films.why: Topped critics' polls of the 21st century for its dreamlike command of form.

films.title: The Passion of Joan of Arc
films.synopsis: Joan of Arc faces a church tribunal in Rouen. The film follows her interrogation almost entirely in close-up.
films.why: A landmark of the close-up and of performance in silent cinema.

films.title: Sunset Blvd.
films.synopsis: A struggling screenwriter is drawn into the mansion of a forgotten silent-film star in Hollywood.
films.why: The sharpest film about the industry that made it.

films.title: Bicycle Thieves
films.synopsis: In postwar Rome, a man needs his bicycle to keep a new job. When it is stolen, he and his young son search the city.
films.why: Won the first Sight & Sound poll in 1952 and defined neorealism.

films.title: Mirror
films.synopsis: A dying poet recalls his childhood, his mother and the turbulence of the century. Memory, dream and newsreel run together.
films.why: Tarkovsky's most personal film and a model of poetic, nonlinear narrative.

films.title: L'Atalante
films.synopsis: A young barge captain marries a village girl and brings her aboard. Life on the canal tests the new marriage.
films.why: Vigo's only feature; a poetic-realist touchstone for later directors.

films.title: Breathless
films.synopsis: A small-time thief on the run in Paris stays close to an American student. The police close in as he tries to collect money owed.
films.why: Launched the French New Wave with jump cuts and street shooting.

films.title: Au hasard Balthazar
films.synopsis: A donkey passes among the owners of a French village over the course of its life. The film observes the people around it.
films.why: Bresson's austere masterwork; admired by Godard, Tarkovsky and many others.

films.title: Beau travail
films.synopsis: A former French Foreign Legion officer remembers his time commanding soldiers in Djibouti and the arrival of a new recruit.
films.why: Ranked in the Sight & Sound top ten in 2022.

films.title: The Night of the Hunter
films.synopsis: A false preacher pursues two children who know where money is hidden. They flee down a river.
films.why: Laughton's only film as director; a cult masterpiece of expressionist style.

films.title: North by Northwest
films.synopsis: An advertising executive is mistaken for a spy and swept into a chase across America.
films.why: The prototype of the wrong-man chase thriller.

films.title: Rashomon
films.synopsis: A crime in a forest is recounted by several witnesses. Their accounts differ in important ways.
films.why: Introduced Japanese cinema to the West and gave a name to a storytelling method.

films.title: The Godfather Part II
films.synopsis: The film alternates between a young immigrant's rise in early New York and his son's attempts to expand the family business.
films.why: Rare sequel regarded as equal to its original.

films.title: The General
films.synopsis: During the Civil War, a railroad engineer sets out alone after his stolen locomotive.
films.why: Keaton's masterpiece, noted for its precise stunts and staging.

films.title: Battleship Potemkin
films.synopsis: Sailors aboard a Russian warship grow resentful of their conditions. Tension spreads from the ship to the port city of Odessa.
films.why: The proving ground of montage theory and its influence on editing.

films.title: Raging Bull
films.synopsis: A middleweight boxer fights his way through the 1940s while his temper strains every relationship he has.
films.why: Voted best film of the 1980s in many critics' polls.

films.title: Playtime
films.synopsis: Tourists and businessmen wander through a gleaming modernist Paris, where signs and glass confuse everyone.
films.why: Tati's monumental satire of modern architecture, built on a full-scale set.

films.title: The 400 Blows
films.synopsis: A restless Parisian schoolboy is misunderstood at school and at home. He drifts into small acts of defiance.
films.why: The breakthrough of the French New Wave and a template for the coming-of-age film.

films.title: Late Spring
films.synopsis: A young woman lives contentedly with her widowed father until relatives urge her to marry.
films.why: The first of Ozu's celebrated postwar family dramas.

films.title: Ordet
films.synopsis: On a Danish farm, a patriarch's family is divided over faith. One son believes himself to be Jesus Christ.
films.why: A pinnacle of spiritual cinema and long-take staging.

films.title: Barry Lyndon
films.synopsis: An Irish rogue in the eighteenth century tries to climb from poverty into high society.
films.why: Celebrated for candlelit cinematography and painterly composition.

films.title: Blade Runner
films.synopsis: In a rain-soaked future Los Angeles, a retired officer is pulled back to hunt escaped artificial humans.
films.why: Defined the look of modern science-fiction.

films.title: M
films.synopsis: A child killer terrorises Berlin. The police and the city's criminals both begin hunting him.
films.why: An early sound masterpiece that helped define the crime thriller.

films.title: Lawrence of Arabia
films.synopsis: A British officer is sent into the Arabian desert during the First World War and becomes involved in an Arab revolt.
films.why: The benchmark of widescreen epic filmmaking.

films.title: La dolce vita
films.synopsis: A journalist drifts through a week of nightlife, scandal and celebrity in Rome. He searches for something more meaningful.
films.why: Won the Palme d'Or and shaped the image of modern Rome and celebrity culture.

films.title: Andrei Rublev
films.synopsis: Episodic scenes follow a medieval icon painter through a violent and turbulent Russia. His faith and his art are repeatedly tested.
films.why: Tarkovsky's epic on the artist's place in history; long suppressed in the USSR.

films.title: The Apartment
films.synopsis: An insurance clerk lends his flat to executives for their affairs, hoping to advance his career.
films.why: Won Best Picture and balanced cynicism with warmth.

films.title: Stalker
films.synopsis: A guide leads a writer and a professor into a forbidden Zone where a room is said to grant wishes.
films.why: One of the most analysed works of slow cinema.

films.title: Do the Right Thing
films.synopsis: On the hottest day of the summer in a Brooklyn neighbourhood, tensions rise around a local pizzeria.
films.why: A landmark of American independent cinema on race and community.

films.title: Shoah
films.synopsis: Over more than nine hours, interviews with survivors, witnesses and perpetrators address the Nazi extermination camps.
films.why: A landmark of testimony-based documentary with no archival footage.

films.title: Contempt
films.synopsis: A screenwriter is hired to rework an adaptation of the Odyssey. His marriage unravels during the production.
films.why: Godard's most lavish film, a meditation on cinema and commerce.

films.title: Modern Times
films.synopsis: A factory worker struggles with machines, joblessness and the Depression, and meets a young woman in similar trouble.
films.why: Chaplin's last appearance as the Tramp and his comment on industrial life.

films.title: The Battle of Algiers
films.synopsis: In 1950s Algeria, an independence movement and French paratroopers fight a hidden war in the city's streets.
films.why: Shot like newsreel; studied by filmmakers and military academies.

films.title: L'avventura
films.synopsis: During a yacht outing, a woman vanishes on a rocky island. Her lover and her friend search for her and drift together.
films.why: Redefined narrative cinema and booed at Cannes before being celebrated.

films.title: GoodFellas
films.synopsis: A boy from Brooklyn grows up around the local mob and rises through its ranks.
films.why: Set a standard for fast, voice-driven crime filmmaking.

films.title: The Third Man
films.synopsis: An American writer arrives in postwar Vienna to meet a friend and finds the friend has died in suspicious circumstances.
films.why: Famed for its angled camerawork and zither score.

films.title: Meshes of the Afternoon
films.synopsis: A woman's afternoon repeats in a dreamlike loop.
films.why: Founding work of the American avant-garde.

films.title: It's a Wonderful Life
films.synopsis: A small-town man's life is reviewed on a night when everything seems to have gone wrong.
films.why: Gained its classic status through decades of rediscovery.

films.title: Chinatown
films.synopsis: A private detective in 1930s Los Angeles takes a routine case that leads into the city's water politics.
films.why: The model neo-noir, often cited for its screenplay.

films.title: Metropolis
films.synopsis: In a vertical city, the son of the ruler befriends a woman who speaks for the workers beneath.
films.why: Defined the visual language of cinematic science fiction.

films.title: Journey to Italy
films.synopsis: An English couple travel to Naples to sell a property. Their marriage shows strain in unfamiliar surroundings.
films.why: A major influence on the French New Wave and modern cinema.

films.title: Ugetsu
films.synopsis: In civil-war Japan, two villagers leave their wives to pursue wealth and glory, and encounter strange events.
films.why: Brought Mizoguchi's ghost-story artistry to the West.

films.title: Touch of Evil
films.synopsis: A Mexican narcotics officer and his wife cross paths with a powerful police captain at the U.S. border after a car explosion.
films.why: Opens with one of cinema's most celebrated tracking shots.

films.title: Jaws
films.synopsis: A police chief, a scientist and a fisherman set out to stop a shark terrorising a summer resort town.
films.why: The first modern blockbuster.

films.title: The Wizard of Oz
films.synopsis: A Kansas girl is swept to a magical land and seeks a way home.
films.why: Technicolor cornerstone of American culture.

films.title: Pierrot le fou
films.synopsis: A bored husband runs away from Paris with his former babysitter and heads south, pursued by trouble.
films.why: Godard's most colourful and freewheeling New Wave film.

films.title: Once Upon a Time in the West
films.synopsis: A widow arrives in a frontier town just as a railroad empire and a hired gunman converge on her land.
films.why: The grand opera of the spaghetti western.

films.title: Rio Bravo
films.synopsis: A sheriff holds a dangerous prisoner in jail while a small group of allies waits for the prisoner's powerful brother.
films.why: Hawks's relaxed ensemble western, beloved by directors such as Tarantino and Carpenter.

films.title: Sans soleil
films.synopsis: Letters from a travelling cameraman reflect on memory, Japan and Africa.
films.why: Cornerstone of the essay film.

films.title: Sansho the Bailiff
films.synopsis: In feudal Japan, two children are separated from their mother and sold into servitude.
films.why: A pinnacle of Mizoguchi's long-take style.

films.title: Sherlock Jr.
films.synopsis: A projectionist dreams himself into the film he is screening.
films.why: Keaton's inventive film-about-film.

films.title: The Leopard
films.synopsis: A Sicilian prince watches his aristocratic world shift during the unification of Italy.
films.why: A sumptuous study of social change; Palme d'Or winner.

films.title: Wild Strawberries
films.synopsis: An elderly professor travels by car to receive an honour. Along the way he revisits scenes from his past.
films.why: One of Bergman's most humane works and a model for reflective road films.

films.title: Nashville
films.synopsis: Twenty-four characters converge around a political campaign and the country-music scene in Nashville.
films.why: The defining ensemble film of the 1970s.

films.title: Ali: Fear Eats the Soul
films.synopsis: An older cleaning woman and a younger Moroccan worker meet and marry in Munich.
films.why: Fassbinder's best-known film.

films.title: Blue Velvet
films.synopsis: A young man finds a severed ear in a field, and he starts investigating a singer in a nearby town.
films.why: Lynch's breakthrough into suburban surrealism.

films.title: The Shining
films.synopsis: A writer takes a winter caretaker job at an isolated hotel with his wife and young son.
films.why: Kubrick's horror landmark, constantly re-evaluated.

films.title: The Piano
films.synopsis: A mute pianist and her daughter arrive in 1850s New Zealand for an arranged marriage.
films.why: First Palme d'Or for a woman director.

films.title: A Man Escaped
films.synopsis: A French Resistance fighter held by the Germans prepares to escape from prison.
films.why: Bresson's pared-down study of process and grace.

films.title: A Woman Under the Influence
films.synopsis: A devoted housewife's unpredictable behaviour strains her marriage and family.
films.why: Cassavetes's landmark of improvisational, performance-driven cinema.

films.title: Cleo from 5 to 7
films.synopsis: A singer spends two hours wandering Paris while she waits for the results of a medical test. The city, and the people she meets in it, slowly change how she sees her own fear.
films.why: A landmark of the French New Wave's Left Bank strand, built almost entirely in real time.

films.title: Fanny and Alexander
films.synopsis: Two children in an early-twentieth-century Swedish family live through a change that brings them under a stern new guardian.
films.why: Bergman's summation of his themes, told on a lavish scale.

films.title: Daisies
films.synopsis: Two young women decide the world is spoiled and misbehave.
films.why: Anarchic landmark of the Czechoslovak New Wave.

films.title: The Wild Bunch
films.synopsis: Ageing outlaws plan a last job in 1913 Texas as the old West fades.
films.why: Changed the depiction of screen violence and the revisionist western.

films.title: Dr. Strangelove
films.synopsis: A rogue American general orders a nuclear attack. In the war room, officials scramble to stop it.
films.why: The defining Cold War satire.

films.title: Madame de…
films.synopsis: A pair of earrings passes from hand to hand through a society woman's life.
films.why: Ophüls's gliding-camera high point.

films.title: The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance
films.synopsis: A senator returns to a small town for a funeral and recounts how his reputation began.
films.why: Ford's reflection on myth-making in the West.

films.title: The Red Shoes
films.synopsis: A young dancer joins a ballet company run by a demanding impresario.
films.why: Technicolor ballet masterpiece.

films.title: The Grand Illusion
films.synopsis: French officers held in a German prison camp during the First World War plan escapes while forming bonds with their captors.
films.why: A humanist landmark; the first foreign-language film nominated for Best Picture.

films.title: Pulp Fiction
films.synopsis: Intertwined stories of hitmen, a boxer and a gangster's wife unfold in Los Angeles.
films.why: Reshaped 1990s independent film and nonlinear storytelling.

films.title: Portrait of a Lady on Fire
films.synopsis: An 18th-century painter is secretly hired to paint a portrait of a reluctant bride-to-be. Over the days they spend together on an isolated island, painter and subject grow close.
films.why: A precise, painterly study of looking and being looked at, widely cited as the century's highest-ranked new film in the 2022 Sight & Sound poll.

films.title: The Spirit of the Beehive
films.synopsis: A girl in 1940s Spain is haunted after a village screening of Frankenstein.
films.why: Touchstone of Spanish cinema.

films.title: A Brighter Summer Day
films.synopsis: A teenager in 1960s Taipei is drawn into street gangs.
films.why: Epic of the Taiwanese New Wave.

films.title: The Conformist
films.synopsis: In 1930s Italy, a man seeking normality takes a government job that sends him abroad.
films.why: Famous for its cinematography, which influenced the New Hollywood generation.

films.title: Children of Paradise
films.synopsis: In nineteenth-century Paris, a mime, an actor and a criminal all love the same woman.
films.why: Made under Occupation conditions; a celebrated epic of French cinema.

films.title: The Mother and the Whore
films.synopsis: An idle young man juggles two women in post-1968 Paris.
films.why: Defining talk-driven French film.

films.title: Wanda
films.synopsis: A drifting woman in Pennsylvania leaves her family and joins a petty criminal.
films.why: Landmark of American independent film.

films.title: Killer of Sheep
films.synopsis: A slaughterhouse worker in 1970s Watts moves through his days numbed by repetitive, grim labor, while scenes of neighborhood children at play unfold around him.
films.why: Shot on a shoestring over several years, it became a touchstone of independent Black American cinema and the L.A. Rebellion movement.

films.title: To Be or Not to Be
films.synopsis: A Warsaw theatre troupe uses its disguises against Nazi occupiers.
films.why: Black comedy far ahead of its time.

films.title: Yi Yi
films.synopsis: A Taipei family faces a series of life changes.
films.why: Top-ranked 21st-century film in several polls.

films.title: Spirited Away
films.synopsis: A girl enters a spirit world's bathhouse to save her parents.
films.why: Won the Oscar and a Golden Bear.

films.title: Come and See
films.synopsis: A Belarusian teenager joins the partisans in 1943.
films.why: Among the most harrowing war films ever made.

films.title: A Matter of Life and Death
films.synopsis: An RAF pilot who cheated death argues for his life.
films.why: Postwar fantasy in colour and monochrome.

films.title: News from Home
films.synopsis: Long static shots of New York City streets and subways play beneath a voiceover reading letters from the filmmaker's mother in Belgium.
films.why: A structural essay-film pairing of image and voice that extends Akerman's interest in duration and distance.

films.title: The Seventh Seal
films.synopsis: A knight returning from the Crusades meets Death and challenges him to a game of chess.
films.why: Brought art-house cinema to a wide international audience.

films.title: Imitation of Life
films.synopsis: Two single mothers, one white and one Black, raise their daughters together.
films.why: Sirk's melodrama on race and ambition.

films.title: Pickpocket
films.synopsis: A young Parisian drifts into petty theft as a test of himself.
films.why: Bresson's spare study of compulsion.

films.title: Bringing Up Baby
films.synopsis: A palaeontologist's life is upended by a madcap heiress and a pet leopard.
films.why: Quintessential screwball comedy.

films.title: Amarcord
films.synopsis: A year in a seaside Italian town of the 1930s is seen through the memories of its residents.
films.why: Fellini's affectionate memory film about fascist-era provincial life.

films.title: Daughters of the Dust
films.synopsis: On a Sea Island off the Georgia coast in 1902, a Gullah family debates whether to migrate north, torn between the pull of the mainland and the ground their ancestors are buried in.
films.why: The first feature by a Black woman director to receive wide U.S. theatrical release, and a formally radical, non-linear family portrait.

films.title: Moonlight
films.synopsis: A boy growing up in a rough Miami neighborhood is shown at three stages of his life, as he comes to terms with his sexuality and his place in the world around him.
films.why: Told in triptych, with a tactile, color-saturated visual style; won the Academy Award for Best Picture.

films.title: Aguirre, the Wrath of God
films.synopsis: Spanish conquistadors descend the Amazon searching for El Dorado.
films.why: Defining film of New German Cinema.

films.title: Gertrud
films.synopsis: A woman in early-1900s Copenhagen demands a love without compromise.
films.why: Dreyer's austere final film.

films.title: La Jetee
films.synopsis: After a nuclear war has devastated the world, an underground experiment sends a prisoner back through his own memory in search of a way to save the future.
films.why: A science-fiction film told almost entirely in still photographs; its central image later inspired Terry Gilliam's 12 Monkeys.

films.title: The Gleaners and I
films.synopsis: A filmmaker travels the French countryside and cities meeting people who gather what others throw away, from leftover crops to discarded furniture, and turns her camera on her own aging hands along the way.
films.why: A warm, self-reflexive documentary essay that treats the act of filming as its own kind of gleaning.

films.title: Don't Look Now
films.synopsis: A grieving couple in Venice meet a psychic who claims to see their daughter.
films.why: Landmark of fragmented editing.

films.title: My Neighbor Totoro
films.synopsis: Two young sisters move with their father to a house in the countryside while their mother recovers from illness in hospital, and discover gentle forest spirits living nearby.
films.why: A gentle, unhurried animated film that became a defining work of Studio Ghibli and a symbol of the studio itself.

films.title: Celine and Julie Go Boating
films.synopsis: A librarian and a magician strike up a friendship in Paris, and together they begin slipping into a haunted house where the same melodramatic story keeps replaying itself.
films.why: A playful, three-hour plunge into storytelling and performance that mixes slapstick with genuine mystery.

films.title: Satantango
films.synopsis: On a collapsing collective farm, the residents wait out a long rainy season for the return of a man they believe will save them, unaware of what he actually intends.
films.why: A seven-and-a-half-hour film built from extremely long takes, widely regarded as a defining work of slow cinema.

films.title: Histoire(s) du cinema
films.synopsis: Across eight chapters made over more than a decade, a filmmaker assembles a personal history of cinema out of film clips, paintings, music, and his own commentary.
films.why: A sprawling video-essay project that treats film history itself as raw material for montage.

films.title: Chungking Express
films.synopsis: Two lonely Hong Kong policemen, in loosely connected stories, drift through late-night diners and crowded streets after being left by the women they loved.
films.why: Shot quickly between larger productions, it crystallized Wong's handheld, pop-scored romantic style.

films.title: The Magnificent Ambersons
films.synopsis: A wealthy family's heir resists change as industry transforms an Indiana town.
films.why: Studio-recut masterpiece, often called cinema's great lost film.

films.title: Parasite
films.synopsis: A poor family schemes its way into employment with a wealthy household, one fake credential at a time, until a buried secret in the house upends everything.
films.why: A tonal high-wire act between comedy, thriller and class satire; the first non-English-language film to win the Best Picture Oscar.

films.title: Get Out
films.synopsis: A young Black man visits his white girlfriend's family estate for the first time and senses something is deeply wrong beneath the family's warm welcome.
films.why: A horror film that turned racial anxiety into genre mechanics, launching Peele as a major directorial voice.

films.title: Ikiru
films.synopsis: A bureaucrat learns he has little time left and wonders how to use it.
films.why: Kurosawa's deepest humanist drama.

films.title: Notorious
films.synopsis: A U.S. agent recruits a woman to infiltrate a group of exiles in Rio.
films.why: Hitchcock's romance-thriller peak.

films.title: Vagabond
films.synopsis: A young drifter is found dead in a ditch in rural France. Through interviews with the people she crossed paths with in her final weeks, the film pieces together her last days without ever fully explaining her.
films.why: Told backward from a death already announced, refusing the sentimentality that subject usually invites.

films.title: Once Upon a Time in America
films.synopsis: Decades in the lives of Jewish-American gangsters in New York.
films.why: Leone's elegiac final epic.

films.title: Alien
films.synopsis: A space crew investigates a distress signal.
films.why: Defined science-fiction horror.

films.title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
films.synopsis: On its final night of business, a crumbling Taipei movie palace shows one last film to a scattering of patrons while the box office clerk and projectionist drift through the building's empty corridors.
films.why: An almost wordless elegy for communal moviegoing, shot in a real cinema shortly before its closure.

films.title: There Will Be Blood
films.synopsis: A prospector builds an oil empire in early-1900s California.
films.why: Leading film of the 2000s.

films.title: His Girl Friday
films.synopsis: An editor tries to win back his ex-wife and star reporter.
films.why: Fastest overlapping dialogue of classic comedy.

films.title: Last Year at Marienbad
films.synopsis: At a baroque hotel, a man insists he met a woman there last year.
films.why: Modernist puzzle-film landmark.

films.title: All About Eve
films.synopsis: An ageing stage star takes a devoted young fan under her wing.
films.why: Razor-sharp backstage drama.

films.title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
films.synopsis: A group of friends road-tripping through rural Texas stumble onto an isolated farmhouse where a family of killers awaits them.
films.why: A low-budget horror film whose raw, documentary-like texture reshaped the genre's visual grammar.

films.title: The Thing
films.synopsis: A research team at an Antarctic outpost discovers a shape-shifting alien life form that can perfectly imitate any living thing, and begins turning on each other out of pure suspicion.
films.why: Its practical creature effects and bleak, paranoid tone have made it one of the most influential horror films of its decade.

films.title: The Matrix
films.synopsis: A computer programmer is pulled into a hidden resistance movement after learning the world he knows is a simulated reality built to keep humanity docile.
films.why: Fused martial-arts choreography, philosophy, and pioneering visual effects into a genre-defining blockbuster.

films.title: The Umbrellas of Cherbourg
films.synopsis: A young couple in a French port town faces separation. All dialogue is sung.
films.why: Palme d'Or winner.

films.title: Star Wars
films.synopsis: A farm boy joins a rebellion against a galactic empire.
films.why: Transformed popular cinema.

films.title: Only Angels Have Wings
films.synopsis: A traveling entertainer arrives at a remote South American port town and falls in with a crew of mail pilots who fly dangerous routes through the mountains.
films.why: A defining Hawksian study of professional competence and quiet courage under pressure.

films.title: Johnny Guitar
films.synopsis: A saloon owner on the edge of a frontier town faces down a posse led by a rival woman determined to run her out, while a gunfighter from her past arrives to help.
films.why: A stylized, operatic Western built around two fierce female leads, later reclaimed as a landmark of camp and queer subtext.

films.title: The Colour of Pomegranates
films.synopsis: The life of the 18th-century Armenian poet Sayat-Nova is told not through conventional narrative but through a sequence of symbolic tableaux drawn from Armenian folk art and iconography.
films.why: One of cinema's most radical breaks from narrative convention, composed almost entirely of static, symbolic tableaux.

films.title: Vivre sa vie
films.synopsis: Twelve episodes follow a young Parisian woman's life.
films.why: Godard's portrait of Anna Karina.

films.title: Annie Hall
films.synopsis: A comedian looks back on his relationship with a singer.
films.why: Reshaped the romantic comedy.

films.title: Hiroshima mon amour
films.synopsis: A French actress and a Japanese architect have an affair in Hiroshima.
films.why: Founding work of modernist cinema.

films.title: The Ascent
films.synopsis: Two Soviet partisans are captured by German forces during World War II, and must each decide, under brutal pressure, what they are and are not willing to betray.
films.why: A harrowing war film shaped by religious imagery, made by one of Soviet cinema's few prominent woman directors.

films.title: The Gold Rush
films.synopsis: The Tramp joins the Klondike gold rush and meets hunger, danger and a dance-hall girl.
films.why: Chaplin's definitive silent comedy.

films.title: Los Olvidados
films.synopsis: Street children in Mexico City struggle to survive.
films.why: Buñuel's Mexican breakthrough.
